The Story of King Bheem

I bow to Lord Jina, the bestower of all happiness, and I write the story of Bheemraj, which inspires noble souls to feel detachment from this world of suffering.

In the city of Kampilya, there was a king named Bheem. This evil-minded man was a great sinner. His queen was Somshri, and they had a son named Bheemdas. Following tradition, Bheem had a proclamation made at Nandishwar Mountain that no one should commit violence against any living being during the festival. The king made the proclamation, but he himself was deeply lustful. He could not go a single day without eating meat. During the festival, he ordered his cooks to prepare meat for him. But the shops were closed, so he was greatly worried. Where would he get meat?

Then he devised a scheme. He brought a dead child from the cremation ground and had it cooked. The king found the meat very delicious. He asked the cooks, "Why is this meat so much tastier than usual?" The cooks, frightened, told him the truth. The king then said, "From now on, cook only children's meat for me."

The king had spoken the order easily, but the cooks were deeply troubled. Where would they find children every day? Yet the king's order had to be obeyed. So they devised a plan: every evening, they would go to the neighbourhoods where children were playing, lure them with sweets, seize one quickly, and bring him back. In this way, the cook began taking children's lives daily. Truly, the company of sinners makes others sinful too. Just as King Bheem was a sinner, his cook became equally wicked through his company.

Children began disappearing daily, and the city was in an uproar. Everyone tried to find out what was happening. One day, the cook quietly seized a householder's child and was leaving when someone saw him. The cook was caught immediately. When questioned, he told the whole truth. The matter reached the ministers. They made Bheemdas the king and banished Bheem and the cook from the city. Truly, no one supports sinners. Mother, son, brother, sister, friend, minister, subjects — all abandon the sinner.

Bheem, now exiled, wandered in the forest with his cook. There, through the ripening of his sins, he was attacked by wild animals and killed. The cook too perished miserably. Both fell into hell, where they suffered for countless ages.

This story teaches that the company of sinners is deadly. Bheem's wickedness corrupted not only himself but also his cook, and both perished miserably. And the sin of killing innocent children is among the gravest of all. The wise should avoid the company of the wicked and cultivate compassion for all living beings.
